# IRIS MCP Agent Skills Pack

This directory is **generated** from the suite's MCP `prompts` capability (Epic 25). Each skill's body is the text `prompts/get` renders for the prompt of the same name. Its `description` is the prompt's separate model-invocation description, and `metadata.iris-tools-preset` is its tool preset; both are set in the prompt's `skill` field in `packages/<server>/src/prompts/`. The skills pack catalog, `packages/client-config/skills-pack/README.md`, lists these skills with the knowledge skills and the always-on rule.

## Installation

Copy the skill directories you want into your project's `.claude/skills/` directory (or point your client's skill-loader configuration at this `skills/` directory directly):

```bash
cp -r skills/<skill-name> /path/to/your/project/.claude/skills/
```

Each skill is a self-contained `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata`) followed by the workflow instructions — the exact tool sequence, argument names, and safety notes an MCP client should follow. Tool names referenced in every skill are validated against the live tool catalog by `scripts/validate-prompts.mjs` (wired into the default test suite), so a renamed or removed tool breaks CI rather than shipping a broken skill.

## Available Skills

| Skill | Server | Tool preset | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check-system-health` | iris-ops-mcp | `full` | Runs one composite health check of an IRIS instance across its nine areas (journal, databases, license, locks, alerts, mirror, ECP, interoperability and the system) and follows each warning, critical or error finding to the tool that explains or fixes it, never running a destructive fix without the user's confirmation. Use when the user asks whether IRIS is healthy or wants a health or status check, or reports trouble with journal space, database size, the license, locks or alerts. |
| `run-external-backup` | iris-ops-mcp | `full` | Freezes an IRIS instance for an external backup snapshot taken at the OS or SAN level, waits while the user takes the snapshot, and always thaws the instance afterwards, even when the snapshot fails, then confirms that journaling resumed and checks the run in the backup history. Use when the user wants to back up IRIS with an external OS-level or SAN snapshot, or asks to freeze and thaw IRIS database writes for a backup. |
| `diagnose-slow-query` | iris-dev-mcp | `developer` | Diagnoses a slow IRIS SQL query from its query plan, the maps and indexes the plan reads, and the statement's cumulative run-time statistics, looking for full table scans, missing indexes, hot statements and plan inefficiencies, then recommends a fix such as a new index or a rewritten WHERE clause without applying it. Use when the user says a SQL query is slow, asks why a query does not use an index, or wants a query plan explained. |
| `deploy-and-test-class` | iris-dev-mcp | `developer` | Deploys an ObjectScript class or package from local source files to IRIS with a glob-path load and compile, fixes compile errors in the source and loads it again, runs its unit tests, compares the returned total with the number of test methods because an early partial result looks like a green run, re-attaches to a run that is still going instead of starting a second one, and measures line coverage when the user asks for it. Use when the user wants to deploy, load or import ObjectScript source into IRIS, compile it, run its %UnitTest tests, or see their coverage. |
| `promote-environment-change` | iris-dev-mcp | `developer` | Promotes configuration and code drift from one IRIS environment to another in review-before-write order, diff -> plan -> confirmed execute -> second diff: it compares mappings, System Default Settings, web applications, supported CPF settings and, given a spec, ObjectScript source, executes only the plan steps the user picks and confirms, and checks that the promoted drift is gone. It never removes an item that exists only on the target. Use when the user wants to compare two IRIS servers or environments, or to promote, sync or copy changes from one to another, such as from development to test. |
| `edit-and-test-class` | iris-dev-mcp | `core` | Changes a few lines of an ObjectScript class directly in IRIS: reads only the lines around the change, applies a guarded line edit that stores nothing when the class no longer matches what was read, compiles the class and fixes errors the same way, runs its unit tests and checks the returned total, and reports the diff. Use when the user wants a small fix or change to a class that lives in IRIS, especially one with no local source file, or asks to patch, compile and test a class in place. |
| `trace-message-flow` | iris-interop-mcp | `core` | Traces one interoperability message flow from a session or message header ID: lists every hop, searches the session's message headers, reads the bodies that matter under the PHI data policy, draws a sequence diagram, and pulls the error log entries of each failing item, then reports where the flow failed and recommends next steps without running a recovery. Use when the user asks what happened to a message or session, why a message failed or never arrived, or how a message moved through an IRIS interoperability production. |
| `recover-stuck-production` | iris-interop-mcp | `core` | Diagnoses and recovers a troubled or wedged interoperability production along an escalation ladder, in order: status, queues and error logs first, then the recover action, and the clean action only when recover does not fix it, never wiping persistent business state unless the user explicitly accepts the data loss. Use when an IRIS interoperability production is stuck, troubled or suspended, messages are not processing or queues are backing up, or the user asks to restart or recover a production. |
| `resend-failed-messages` | iris-interop-mcp | `core` | Resends failed interoperability messages for one configuration item, dry run first: it previews the match count and a sample, resends only after the user approves with an explicit confirmation, and then checks the new message headers. It states that a resend delivers the data downstream again and that the resend actions are writes disabled by default. Use when the user wants to retry, replay or resend failed or errored messages in an IRIS interoperability production. |
| `find-patient-messages` | iris-interop-mcp | `core` | Finds a patient's interoperability messages by an identifier such as a medical record number, through a Search Table and in search windows of at most 7 days, lists the matching message headers, and reads message bodies only when the user wants the content, under the PHI data policy, which redacts or withholds them. Use when the user asks for the messages, HL7 traffic or message history of a patient or medical record number in an IRIS interoperability production. |
| `provision-project-environment` | iris-admin-mcp | `core` | Provisions a new IRIS project environment in order: a DATA and a CODE database, a namespace over them, a user whose default namespace it is, and a web application, checking each step before the next, rolling back the completed steps when one fails, and naming the manual follow-up a new web application needs. Use when the user wants to set up or create a new IRIS project, namespace or application environment. |
| `audit-security-posture` | iris-admin-mcp | `full` | A read-only audit of an IRIS instance's security: users whose password settings look stale or that may use a well-known default credential, every user and role that holds %All, services that are enabled without authentication or not needed, SSL/TLS configurations with a minimum TLS version below 1.2 or missing certificate paths, and whether auditing is on, ending in a report of recommended fixes; it changes nothing. Use when the user asks to audit, review or harden IRIS security, asks who holds %All, or asks whether services, SSL/TLS or auditing are set up safely. |

Prefer calling these workflows via the MCP `prompts` capability directly (`prompts/get`) when your client supports it — the skill files here are a convenience export for clients that only load local skill directories.
